Overview[]

In Swordburst 2, there are 6 different main weapon types — longswords, greatswords, rapiers, katanas, spears and scythes. There are some variants on these base types but they do not affect the major combat mechanics, just range and cosmetic appeal.

The main weapon types have different attack styles and ranges, varying on each weapon.

Rarity[]

Rarity for items determines two things. The drop chance (excluding most burst items), and how many times the item can be upgraded. Generally speaking, rarities also indicate the "Max level" of a floor, such as the legendary drops on floor 9 indicating that level 85 was the max level at the time of floor 9's release.

Upgrades (see Upgrade Crystal) for rarities are as follow:

  • Commons and Uncommons can be upgraded to +10
  • Rares can be upgraded to +15
  • Legendaries and Tributes can be upgraded to +20
  • Bursts can be upgraded to +25

The drop chances for each rarity significantly increase in difficulty to drop. To learn more about drop chances see Mobs/Drops and Chests.

Auras

Auras are equippable cosmetic items, obtainable through Aura Chests, Burst Store, and trading.

They do not provide additional stats; they are only cosmetics to customize the look of your character and gear.

Longswords

Longswords are single-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 12%. You can also use 2 swords at once, but the damage will be an average of the 2 swords if they are different variants or upgrade levels.

The attack pattern for this weapon strikes at an angle two times and then strikes at an angle in the opposite direction. (45-45-45)

  • The Dual Wield is a counterpart of the longsword class. It uses 2 longswords at once that strike with much more range (180-180-360).
  • Longswords lack range when compared to other weapons.
  • Sub-categorical weapon classes of the Longsword include Axes, Daggers, Fans, and Hammers.
    • There are more sub-categories for Longswords than any other weapon type.
  • If you choose to dual wield two Longswords, the damage is calculated by what you have equipped in each hand. Your total damage per hit is 60% of your Right Hand's sword damage plus 40% of your Left Hand's sword damage. Crit chance is also calculated this way, but boosts still add up. For the best results, avoid dual-wielding two longswords with different damages. Instead, just use the stronger of the two alone, aside from if the increased skill damage and atack radius are extremely important.
    • Note: if you dual wield two of the exact same weapon, the damage will be the same as it would be if you were single wielding it. Critical Chance and attack speed are NOT increased if you choose to Dual Wield, instead your Damage and Crit will be 60% of your Right Hand and 40% of your Left Hand. The only major change is your attack radius and the sum of the regeneration boosts from each sword. This also means you will always lose damage if you use a stronger sword with a weaker one in your left, instead of just single wielding the stronger one.

Hammers/Axes/Scythes

Hammers, Axes, and Scythes are single-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 12%.

  • These weapons function exactly like Longswords, with the exception of model size and hitboxes.

Daggers/Fans/Discs/Pillars/Fists

Daggers, Fans, Discs, Pillars, and Fists are single-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 12%. The attack pattern for these weapons strikes at an angle two times, then strikes downwards. (45-45-0)

  • These weapons function exactly like Longswords, with the exception of model size and hitboxes.
  • Currently, there is only one pillar-type weapon in the game, being Formaug's Demise.
  • Currently, there is only one 'fist'-type weapon in the game, being Fist.


Crosses

Crosses are single-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 12%. Currently, there is only one cross-type weapon in the game, being Redeemer.

  • This class of weapon is functionally identical to longswords.



Pros:

Cons:

  • Medium Critical Chance (12%)
  • Single 1H - decent skill damage multiplier (3x)
  • Dual Wield - high skill damage multiplier (3.3x,/5x)
  • Dual Wield - great area of effect (180-180-360)
  • Dual Wield - can stack regeneration stats
  • Mediocre range
  • Dual Wield - cannot stack damage/critical chance
  • Dual Wield - strongest skill (Infinity Slash) is unobtainable by normal means
  • Dual Wield - if two longswords have different damage outputs, it is always less than the stronger variant.
  • Dual Wield - if dual-wielding the same longsword, both must be maxed out for the maximum damage output, else it's weaker than just using the stronger of the two.

Greatswords

Greatswords are two-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 18%.

The attack pattern for this weapon strikes sideways two times before slashing downwards. (180-180-0)

  • When the Berserker Animation Pack is equipped, the attacks cover much more range. (180-360-360)
  • Sub-categorical weapon classes of the Greatsword include Scythes, Hammers, and Axes.

Hammers and Axes are two-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 18%.

  • These weapons function exactly like Greatswords, with the exception of model size and hitboxes.


Pros:

Cons:

  • High Critical Chance (18%)

  • Berserker animation pack hits downwards very well.
  • Low skill damage multiplier (2.75x)
  • Dynamic animations provide little range when using the Berserker animation pass.
  • Berserker animation pack can barely hit upwards.

Katanas

Katanas are two-handed weapons that have a hit rate of 16 times per 10 seconds. They have a critical chance of 15%.

The attack pattern for this weapon strikes sideways two times, then pushes forward. (180-180-0)

  • This weapon has no counterparts.
  • With the Ninja Animation Pack, it increases frontal range and provides a wider attack. (60-180-60)



Pros:

Cons:

  • High skill damage multiplier (3.3x)
  • Decent critical chance (15%)
  • Great area of effect with the Ninja animation pack (60-180-60)
  • Leaping Slash consumes little stamina
  • Default animations hit upwards very well
  • Ninja animation pack hits downwards very well
  • Default animations may not always register hits correctly

Armor is equipped by a player to increase their defense. In this game, unusually, defense does not actually decrease damage taken. Instead, it increases the wearer's HP. Accessories

Accessories are equipable items, usually obtained from mobs or from Burst Store purchases. Up to two accessories may be equipped simultaneously. Some accessories provide bonuses, such as added defense or regeneration, though many do not and are purely cosmetic. When multiple accessories are equipped, their effects do stack, including when two of the same accessory are equipped.

Vanity is a feature that lets players change how their accessories look without affecting their stats. This means you can equip an item for its appearance while still keeping the Stats of a different, stronger item.
For example:
If your best shield is Apotheosis, but you also own a body aura that you like the look of, you can equip the body aura as a vanity item on your shield slot. You will look like you’re using the aura, but you will keep the stats of the Apotheosis shield.

In Short : Vanity = look of one item + stats of another.

  • Note: Stamina Regeneration and Health Regeneration from accessories are capped at 250%.

Shields

Shields are a specific type of accessory that provides large amounts of defence and some regen when equipped. They are generally dropped by bosses, with several exceptions.

Body Auras

Body Auras are equippable accessory items, obtainable through aura chests from the Burst Store and trading. They do not provide additional stats; they are only cosmetics.
